title: The Power of Moments: Why Certain Experiences Have Extraordinary Impact

audiences: Leaders, teachers, clinicians, service designers, facilitators, and managers who shape other people's experiences
People planning transitions, milestones, celebrations, feedback, onboarding, recovery from a setback, or a meaningful gathering
Families and teams seeking a practical language for recognition, novelty, courage, purpose, and connection
Readers who prefer memorable cases and design prompts to a technical psychology text

sources.title: The Power of Moments
sources.supports: Canonical identity, publication, ISBN, format, authors, argument, sample, framework, examples, and selected reception.

sources.title: The Power of Moments
sources.author_or_publisher: Chip Heath and Dan Heath; Simon & Schuster via Google Books
sources.supports: Book identity, authors, ISBN, length, full contents, subjects, and searchable preview.
sources.limitations: Limited preview rather than uninterrupted full text.

sources.title: The Power of Moments, Chapter 1: Defining Moments
sources.supports: Primary definitions, peak-end framing, four elements, scope, and Senior Signing Day example.

sources.title: The Power of Moments for Friends and Family
sources.supports: Author-supplied applications of transitions, novelty, peaks, milestones, pride, insight, and connection outside business.
sources.limitations: Companion application guide, not independent evidence.

sources.title: When More Pain Is Preferred to Less: Adding a Better End
sources.author_or_publisher: Daniel Kahneman, Barbara Fredrickson, Charles Schreiber, and Donald Redelmeier; Psychological Science
sources.supports: Experimental evidence that retrospective evaluation of an aversive episode can overweight peak and ending and underweight duration.
sources.limitations: Short aversive laboratory experiences; generalisation to long, positive, complex life experiences is limited.

sources.title: Understanding the reminiscence bump: A systematic review
sources.author_or_publisher: Khadeeja Munawar, Sara K. Kuhn, and Shamsul Haque; PLOS One
sources.supports: Systematic evidence that autobiographical recall often disproportionately represents youth and early adulthood, with timing dependent on cues and memory type.
sources.limitations: Explains recall distributions, not how to manufacture meaningful experiences.

sources.title: The Experimental Generation of Interpersonal Closeness
sources.author_or_publisher: Arthur Aron et al.; Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin
sources.supports: Preliminary experiments showing that escalating reciprocal self-disclosure can generate felt interpersonal closeness in a controlled setting.
sources.limitations: Small, structured experimental interactions; does not create friendship or love on command and does not establish durable relationship quality.

sources.title: How to make even a boring work meeting more memorable
sources.supports: Dan Heath's explanation of transitions, milestones, pits, onboarding, elevation, work applications, and intended purpose.
sources.limitations: Promotional author interview with unverified organisational outcome claims.

sources.title: The Power of Moments
sources.supports: Independent assessment of structure, tone, cases, clinics, practicality, and heuristic character.
sources.limitations: Concise trade review rather than an evidence audit.

sources.title: The Power of Moments
sources.supports: Independent summary and criticism of corporate emphasis and the unresolved authenticity of engineered moments.
sources.limitations: Short review; does not test interventions.

sources.title: The Power of Moments
sources.supports: Clinical practitioner's assessment of relevance to patients, staff, leaders, colleagues, and family.
sources.limitations: Brief book review, not clinical outcome evidence.

sources.title: The Power of Moments
sources.supports: Large reader aggregate and recurring praise for accessible applications alongside concerns about corporate framing, repetition, and feasibility.
sources.limitations: Self-selected, mutable, merged editions, and no control for expertise or completion.

workflow.coverage_notes: Full contents, first chapter, author companion guide, searchable preview, author interview, three relevant research sources, three independent professional or specialist reviews, and a large reader aggregate cover the argument and all parts. No unauthorised full text was used.
